precedent_correction.statement: Any prior approval or guidance treating --sandbox, --dangerously-skip-permissions, cwd=worktree, --add-dir, post-execution source checks, or cache cleanup as sufficient isolation is withdrawn. Astra Steps 2, 6, and 9 require an audited enforcement boundary covering native file tools, descendants, shared Git metadata, trusted state, and delayed writers. That boundary is absent and unproven.

actual_achieved_step_boundary.description: No Astra migration increment is fully conformant. Step 1 is incomplete, Step 2 is unproven, and production AgyBuilder work was implemented ahead of both prerequisites.

sequence_violation.evidence: Commit 872e4fb switched the production default to AgyBuilder before later isolation-labelled commits, while the Step 2 contract, fixtures, and enforcement boundary remain absent.

critical_findings.finding: There is no execution-isolation boundary. AgyBuilder launches unrestricted Windows AGY with inherited environment and host access. The installed AGY help describes --sandbox as terminal restrictions; it does not prove containment of native file tools, descendants, shared Git metadata, trusted run state, hooks, MCP, plugins, or unrelated host files.
evidence: The command combines --sandbox and --dangerously-skip-permissions and relies on cwd, --add-dir, and prompt instructions.

critical_findings.finding: Builder calls are not durably reserved or centralized. Initial build and all repair/rework routes call self.builder.run directly. Crashes can replay work and replenish in-memory budgets.
evidence: No _dispatch_builder, builder_calls_used, attempt-state machine, non_resumable enforcement, or OS-backed lock exists.

critical_findings.finding: Post-run source checks cannot prevent external damage and do not prove preservation. The full-status comparison uses path-set differences, so changing the contents of a previously dirty or untracked out-of-scope source file can remain undetected. Linked worktrees retain shared Git metadata.
evidence: Only labels beginning with after_builder receive the additional full-status path comparison.
No content-hash boundary or Git common-directory isolation exists.

critical_findings.finding: The cleanup design directly contradicts Astra. It broadly exempts .agy and .gemini paths from scope rejection and then deletes untracked files based largely on filename suffix. This can erase user or malicious evidence and make a scope violation disappear.

The Builder runtime and result protocol are not the planned protocol. Generic subprocess.run captures text in memory, has no concurrent bounded drains or process-tree ownership, can expose the prompt-bearing argv in timeout errors, and does not preserve partial raw evidence. AgyBuilder accepts one JSON object containing status=SUCCESS without initialization, model, cwd, conversation, terminal cardinality, or contradictory-error validation.
evidence: No run_builder_process, parse_agy_event_stream, or BuilderFailure implementation exists.

critical_findings.finding: Crash-safe rollback and commit identity are incomplete. Checkpoint code references base64 without importing it when untracked files exist. Tests are accepted solely by exit code, are not bound to candidate content, and approval records no tested tree, staged tree OID, expected parent, writer-quiescence proof, or post-commit tree verification.

Cutover and documentation deployment are premature. The repository default is AgyBuilder and the installed skill has already been changed, although isolation and acceptance are unapproved. The installed skill is also internally contradictory and still directs slices to Aider.
